description: When the host process dies during Stage 3, the execution branch keeps the executor's commits but has no executions.jsonl summary row. The Stage 3 resume lookup in apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/stages/execute.py (_resumable_partial_branch) and the leftover salvage in flow/partial_salvage.py only consider an execution branch whose latest ledger row is a failure carrying a partial_head, so a branch with commits past the plan tip and no row is ignored: the resume logs 'no failed execution branch carries partial work; starting from the plan tip', cuts a fresh execution branch and loses the work. Uncommitted tracked changes on such a branch (including its executions/E-*.md notes file) can also make the next checkout fail with an opaque 'would be overwritten' exit 1.
goal: On a Stage 3 resume, detect an execution branch of the current plan on origin that has commits past the plan tip and no summary row in executions.jsonl, and adopt it: the executor continues from its tip with the existing 'partial work' prompt, and uncommitted tracked changes on its worktree are committed as labelled partial work first (reuse the salvage in flow/partial_salvage.py) so they never break a checkout. Put the new detection in a new module under apps/sandbox-executor/src/sandbox_executor/flow/ and call it from the existing resume path; do not grow execute.py. A dirty worktree that still blocks a checkout is reported with the blocking file names, not as a bare git exit code. A branch with a summary row (success or failure) behaves exactly as today. The checkpoint's execution branch and id follow the adopted branch so the post-execution ledger lookup uses the id the executor actually wrote.
rationale: A host crash during Stage 3 currently throws away finished executor work and costs a whole new execution; resume should continue from the commits already on the branch.
acceptance_criteria: A resume with an execution branch that has commits past the plan tip and no executions.jsonl row adopts it and passes it to the executor as partial work; a test covers this.
The same case with an uncommitted tracked change on the branch commits that change as labelled partial work first and does not fail the checkout; a test covers this.
A second resume after a new execution id was minted uses the id the executor wrote for the post-execution ledger lookup; a test covers this.
A branch whose latest row is a success or a failure, and a plan with no execution branch, behave exactly as before; existing tests pass unchanged.
A dirty worktree that still blocks a checkout names the blocking files in the error.
No file outside the scope list changes; module budget files and the budget-check scripts are untouched, every new module is at most 350 lines and execute.py does not grow.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' passes.
